clean_source_blocks.text: For Chinese leader Xi Jinping, North Korea is the neighbour China can neither control nor afford to lose. The two sides often describe their relationship as one "forged in blood", a reference to the Korean War. Yet in recent years, mistrust has strained ties. And now Beijing is trying to reassert sway over a strategically vital yet deeply unpredictable partner. China wants stability on its border and influence in Pyongyang, but without being dragged into crises triggered by North Korea's nuclear ambitions. So Xi's visit this week is likely to be less about friendship, more about leverage. Seoul believes he may try to position China as a mediator between North Korea and the United States, but Beijing may have other motives.
Beijing is trying to reassert influence over a strategically vital yet deeply unpredictable partner.

Mao added, “The visit will be an opportunity for the two sides to work together to further advance bilateral ties in keeping with the times, promote the welfare of the two peoples, and contribute more to peace, stability, development and prosperity in the region and beyond.” More details, she said, would be released later. The two leaders met on September 3 and 4 of last year in Beijing when Kim attended the commemoration event of the 80th anniversary of China’s victory in World War II. During that visit, Kim succeeded in securing his leverage by walking alongside Xi during the event. Xi seems to be visiting Pyongyang this time as a response to Kim’s visit last year. Their meeting will also celebrate the 65th anniversary of the Treaty of Friendship, Cooperation and Mutual Assistance between the two countries.

Chinese President Xi Jinping will make a state visit to North Korea from June 8 to 9. On June 5, a spokesperson for the International Department of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China announced, "At the invitation of Kim Jong Un, General Secretary of the Workers' Party of Korea and Chairman of the State Affairs Commission, President Xi will visit North Korea." The Korean Central News Agency also reported that President Xi will visit North Korea at the invitation of Chairman Kim. North Korean State Affairs Commission Chairman Kim Jong Un is seen shaking hands with Chinese President Xi Jinping at the event commemorating the 80th anniversary of China's Victory Day held in Beijing on September 4 last year. [Lähde: BBC World]
For Chinese leader Xi Jinping, North Korea is the neighbour China can neither control nor afford to lose.

The two sides often describe their relationship as one "forged in blood", a reference to the Korean War.

Yet in recent years, mistrust has strained ties. And now Beijing is trying to reassert  sway over a strategically vital yet deeply unpredictable partner.

China wants stability on its border and influence in Pyongyang, but without being dragged into crises triggered by North Korea's nuclear ambitions.

So Xi's visit this week is likely to be less about friendship, more about leverage.

Seoul believes he may try to position China as a mediator between North Korea and the United States, but Beijing may have other motives.

Western diplomatic sources tell the BBC that China has become increasingly concerned about the growing partnership between Pyongyang and Moscow.

After meeting Russian leader Vladimir Putin last week, Xi may want to ensure he also keeps North Korean leader Kim Jong Un in check, especially as Beijing increases its presence on the global stage.

The cooling between Beijing and Pyongyang was visible, even if subtle.

They barely marked the 75th anniversary of diplomatic relations in October 2024. Public messaging was muted.

China's ambassador did not attend North Korea's founding celebrations the previous month. There were no senior level exchanges throughout the year, a stark contrast with Pyongyang's increasingly warm relationship with Moscow.

That growing closeness with Russia has unsettled Beijing.

After Russia's invasion of Ukraine, North Korea has expanded military cooperation with Putin, culminating in a mutual defence pact that was signed during Putin's visit to Pyongyang in 2024.

About 2,300 North Korean soldiers have died fighting for Russia against Ukraine, according to a BBC investigation. Pyongyang is also accused of supplying ammunition for Russia's war effort in exchange for oil and aid, a development that has alarmed Washington and its allies, and quietly rattled China.

[Lähde: The Diplomat]
According to North Korea’s state-controlled Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) on June 5, Chinese leader Xi Jinping will head to Pyongyang, the capital of North Korea, on June 8 for a summit meeting with North Korea’s autocratic leader Kim Jong Un. The visit was also confirmed by China’s state news agency, Xinhua.

It will be Xi’s first visit to Pyongyang since 2019, and just his second visit overall since coming to power in late 2012.

No details of Xi’s schedule during his two-day visit to Pyongyang have been released. When asked for the “program of the visit” in the daily press conference on June 5, Chinese Foreign Minister spokesperson Mao Ning merely replied that “the two top party and state leaders will exchange views on bilateral relations and issues of mutual interest.”

Mao added, “The visit will be an opportunity for the two sides to work together to further advance bilateral ties in keeping with the times, promote the welfare of the two peoples, and contribute more to peace, stability, development and prosperity in the region and beyond.” More details, she said, would be released later.

The two leaders met on September 3 and 4 of last year in Beijing when Kim attended the commemoration event of the 80th anniversary of China’s victory in World War II. During that visit, Kim succeeded in securing his leverage by walking alongside Xi during the event. Xi seems to be visiting Pyongyang this time as a response to Kim’s visit last year. Their meeting will also celebrate the 65th anniversary of the Treaty of Friendship, Cooperation and Mutual Assistance between the two countries.

The scheduled summit between Xi and Kim next week comes less than a month after Xi hosted U.S. President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin in quick succession. In this context, Xi’s visit to Pyongyang implies that he is now consolidating the anti-U.S. trilateral coalition with Russia and North Korea so that he can increase China’s influence over security dynamics in the East Asia region.

According to the state news agency, Kim emphasized again the necessity of bolstering his country’s nuclear capability and showed his firm will to continue to develop advanced nuclear missile programs. payload.title: Xi Jinping matkustaa Pohjois-Koreaan vaikutusvallan ja vakauden varmistamiseksi
payload.summary: Kiinan presidentti Xi Jinping tekee valtiovierailun Pohjois-Koreaan 8.–9. kesäkuuta Kim Jong-unin kutsusta. Vierailu korostaa maiden läheisiä mutta jännitteisiä suhteita sekä Pekingin pyrkimystä vahvistaa vaikutusvaltaansa Pyongyangissa.
payload.content:
Kiinan presidentti Xi Jinping tekee valtiovierailun Pohjois-Koreaan 8.–9. kesäkuuta Pohjois-Korean johtajan Kim Jong-unin kutsusta. Vierailu ajoittuu tilanteeseen, jossa Peking pyrkii vahvistamaan vaikutusvaltaansa strategisesti tärkeään mutta arvaamattomana pidettyyn naapuriinsa ja samalla välttämään joutumista Pohjois-Korean ydinohjelmaan liittyvien kriisien osapuoleksi.

## Suhde on läheinen mutta epäluulon sävyttämä

Kiina ja Pohjois-Korea kuvaavat usein suhdettaan historiallisesti poikkeuksellisen läheiseksi. Taustalla on Korean sota, johon maiden yhteistä suhdetta koskevissa kuvauksissa viitataan yhä. Viime vuosina maiden välejä on kuitenkin rasittanut epäluottamus, vaikka Pekingille Pohjois-Korea on edelleen naapuri, jota se ei voi hallita mutta jota se ei myöskään halua menettää vaikutuspiiristään.

Kiinan keskeinen tavoite on vakaus omalla rajallaan. Samalla se haluaa säilyttää vaikutusvaltansa Pyongyangissa ilman, että Pohjois-Korean ydintavoitteet vetävät Kiinaa mukaan uusiin kriiseihin. Etelä-Koreassa on arvioitu, että Xi voisi pyrkiä asemoimaan Kiinaa välittäjäksi Pohjois-Korean ja Yhdysvaltojen välille, mutta Pekingin motiivit voivat olla laajemmatkin.

## Vierailu seuraa Kimin Pekingin-matkaa

Vierailusta ilmoitettiin 5. kesäkuuta Kiinan kommunistisen puolueen kansainvälisen osaston kautta. Ilmoituksen mukaan Xi matkustaa Pohjois-Koreaan Kim Jong-unin kutsusta. Myös Pohjois-Korean valtiollinen uutistoimisto kertoi Xi Jinpingin saapuvan maahan Kimin kutsumana.

Xi ja Kim tapasivat viimeksi Pekingissä 3.–4. syyskuuta viime vuonna, kun Kim osallistui Kiinan toisen maailmansodan voiton 80-vuotismuistotilaisuuteen. Tuolloin Kimin esiintyminen Xi Jinpingin rinnalla vahvisti hänen asemaansa maiden välisessä asetelmassa.

## Sopimusjuhla antaa matkalle lisämerkityksen

Nyt tehtävää vierailua on kuvattu vastavuoroiseksi eleeksi Kimin viime vuoden Pekingin-matkalle. Tapaamiseen liittyy myös maiden ystävyys-, yhteistyö- ja keskinäisen avunannon sopimuksen 65-vuotisjuhla.

Kiinan ulkoministeriön edustaja Mao kuvasi vierailua mahdollisuudeksi kehittää kahdenvälisiä suhteita, edistää maiden kansalaisten hyvinvointia sekä tukea rauhaa, vakautta, kehitystä ja vaurautta alueella ja sen ulkopuolella. Lisätietoja vierailun ohjelmasta oli määrä antaa myöhemmin.
summary_bullets: Xi Jinping vierailee Pohjois-Koreassa 8.–9. kesäkuuta Kim Jong-unin kutsusta.
Peking pyrkii vahvistamaan vaikutusvaltaansa Pyongyangissa ja turvaamaan vakauden rajallaan.
Vierailu liittyy myös maiden ystävyys- ja yhteistyösopimuksen 65-vuotisjuhlaan.

Vierailu liittyy myös maiden ystävyys- ja yhteistyösopimuksen 65-vuotisjuhlaan.
article.journalist_note: Artikkeli perustuu annettuihin lähdekatkelmiin. Luokka on korjattu sisällön perusteella ulkomaihin, koska aihe koskee Kiinan ja Pohjois-Korean suhteita.
article.source_text:
For Chinese leader Xi Jinping, North Korea is the neighbour China can neither control nor afford to lose. The two sides often describe their relationship as one "forged in blood", a reference to the Korean War. Yet in recent years, mistrust has strained ties. And now Beijing is trying to reassert sway over a strategically vital yet deeply unpredictable partner. China wants stability on its border and influence in Pyongyang, but without being dragged into crises triggered by North Korea's nuclear ambitions. So Xi's visit this week is likely to be less about friendship, more about leverage. Seoul believes he may try to position China as a mediator between North Korea and the United States, but Beijing may have other motives.

Beijing is trying to reassert influence over a strategically vital yet deeply unpredictable partner.

Mao added, “The visit will be an opportunity for the two sides to work together to further advance bilateral ties in keeping with the times, promote the welfare of the two peoples, and contribute more to peace, stability, development and prosperity in the region and beyond.” More details, she said, would be released later. The two leaders met on September 3 and 4 of last year in Beijing when Kim attended the commemoration event of the 80th anniversary of China’s victory in World War II. During that visit, Kim succeeded in securing his leverage by walking alongside Xi during the event. Xi seems to be visiting Pyongyang this time as a response to Kim’s visit last year. Their meeting will also celebrate the 65th anniversary of the Treaty of Friendship, Cooperation and Mutual Assistance between the two countries.

Chinese President Xi Jinping will make a state visit to North Korea from June 8 to 9. On June 5, a spokesperson for the International Department of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China announced, "At the invitation of Kim Jong Un, General Secretary of the Workers' Party of Korea and Chairman of the State Affairs Commission, President Xi will visit North Korea." The Korean Central News Agency also reported that President Xi will visit North Korea at the invitation of Chairman Kim. North Korean State Affairs Commission Chairman Kim Jong Un is seen shaking hands with Chinese President Xi Jinping at the event commemorating the 80th anniversary of China's Victory Day held in Beijing on September 4 last year.
